problem_statement: themeselection/materio-bootstrap-html-laravel-admin-template-free (Materio) is a polished Bootstrap 5 + Laravel admin template rendered through Blade views: a fixed vertical sidebar menu, a top navbar with a search box and a user dropdown, and an analytics dashboard built from cards — a 'Congratulations Norris' hero, a 'Transactions' card with Sales/Customers/Product/Revenue stats, a 'Weekly Overview' chart, a 'Total Earning' card listing Zipcar/Bitbank/Aviato brands, a 'Sales by Countries' panel, four small metric cards, deposit/withdraw lists, and a users table. Supporting pages include a basic-cards gallery, a buttons reference, and an account-settings form pre-filled with John Doe / john.doe@example.com. Every surface still reads as the generic Materio sales/e-commerce demo. Rework the console into 'Ternpoint Ops', a field-service fleet dispatch operations console, so the dashboard hero, the transactions and earnings cards, the regional panel, the small metric cards, the account-settings identity, the sidebar brand and primary nav label, and the site metadata all tell one coherent dispatch-operations story. Keep Materio's Bootstrap layout, sidebar/navbar chrome, card grid, charts, forms, and Blade/Vite structure intact; only the demo copy and brand should change so the result reads as the same template repurposed for a dispatch operations team rather than a redesign. In addition to the multi-surface rebrand, add a shared "Shift dispatch cadence" rail to the console footer so it renders on every route (dashboard, cards, buttons, account settings): a compact strip with a four-tile metric row (Dispatched today / Crews on shift / Open work orders / SLA met), three shift-band buttons (Morning / Afternoon / Night), and a live readout line that reads "Active dispatch window: <band> — <N> work orders queued". Clicking a shift-band button must re-sync that readout to the selected band and its queued count. The metric row must wrap cleanly with no horizontal overflow on a 390px phone, keep the Materio light card styling, and appear consistently across every page rather than only on the dashboard.
required_content: The dashboard hero card no longer reads 'Congratulations Norris! / Best seller of the month / View Sales' but an operations greeting such as 'On track this week, Priya! / Top dispatcher this month / View Roster'.
The 'Transactions' card is reframed as 'Work Orders' with dispatch-oriented stat labels (Dispatched, Technicians, Open jobs, SLA met) rather than Sales/Customers/Product/Revenue.

The 'Total Earning' card becomes a 'Fleet Utilization' panel whose rows describe real crews/depots (e.g. Northgate Depot, Harbor Route Team, Rapid-Response Crew with van/region subtitles) instead of the Zipcar/Bitbank/Aviato software brands.

The 'Sales by Countries' panel is reframed as 'Jobs by Region', and the small metric cards and weekly chart adopt ops framing (Weekly Dispatch Overview, Jobs Completed, On-time Completion, New Work Orders, Active Shifts).

The account-settings form is personalized to an operations manager persona (first/last name, an @ternpointops email, and 'Ternpoint Ops' as the organization) under an 'Operator Profile' card header instead of the John Doe / ThemeSelection demo defaults.

The sidebar brand wordmark reads 'Ternpoint Ops', the primary sidebar nav label is renamed from 'Dashboards' to 'Operations', the navbar user dropdown reflects the operations persona, and the site metadata (template name/suffix/og title/creator) is rebranded to Ternpoint Ops / Ternpoint Labs while all routes, menus, charts, and forms remain reachable and functional.
The 390px mobile dashboard and the opened mobile sidebar remain readable with no horizontal overflow, and the sidebar/navbar/card chrome keeps its Materio spacing and styling.

A shared 'Shift dispatch cadence' rail is present in the footer on EVERY route (dashboard, cards, buttons, account settings), showing a four-tile metric row (Dispatched today, Crews on shift, Open work orders, SLA met), Morning/Afternoon/Night shift-band buttons, and an 'Active dispatch window: <band> — <N> work orders queued' readout.

Clicking the Afternoon or Night shift-band button re-syncs the readout so it reads 'Active dispatch window: Afternoon' / 'Active dispatch window: Night' with the matching queued count; the previously active band button loses its highlight.
The dispatch-rail metric row wraps with no horizontal overflow at 390px and keeps the Materio light rounded card styling instead of collapsing into a dark unstyled slab.
design_constraints: Preserve Materio's design language: the fixed vertical sidebar menu, top navbar with search and user dropdown, Bootstrap 5 card grid, ApexCharts widgets, form controls, avatars, and the light theme palette and spacing.
Do not restructure the layout, swap the CSS framework, remove the charts/tables/forms, or turn the admin console into a marketing page; it must remain a Bootstrap admin dashboard.

Make edits inside the existing Blade views, the menu JSON, and config/variables.php — resources/views/content/dashboard/dashboards-analytics.blade.php, resources/views/content/pages/pages-account-settings-account.blade.php, resources/menu/verticalMenu.json, the navbar partial, and config/variables.php — rather than adding new pages or client frameworks.
Keep all sidebar menu entries, dashboard routes, the cards/basic and ui/buttons pages, and the account-settings form fields functional; the rename of the primary nav label must not break its route.
New copy must be credible field-service operations content (dispatch, crews, work orders, SLA, regions) grounded in the existing card and form structure, not lorem filler or unrelated domains.
Mobile: the dashboard cards, sidebar, navbar, and account form should keep wrapping cleanly at 390px with no horizontal overflow or collided controls.
The Shift dispatch cadence rail must live in the shared footer partial so it appears on every content route, styled with Materio's light card palette; it must not be limited to the dashboard.
The rail's shift-band interaction must update the live readout DOM in place (no navigation), and the metric row must use a wrapping flex layout so a 390px phone shows no horizontal overflow.
state_constraints: desktop_initial and mobile_initial capture the analytics dashboard home at 1440 and 390px, showing the hero, transactions/earnings cards, regional panel, and small metric cards; the rebrand must land here without breaking the card grid or introducing mobile overflow.
desktop_dashboard_cards captures the dashboard scrolled into the card body so the Work Orders / Fleet Utilization / Jobs by Region content is in view.

desktop_basic_cards and desktop_buttons capture the shared cards and buttons reference pages, which keep the Materio chrome (sidebar, navbar, footer) and must remain reachable and error-free after the nav rename.
desktop_account_settings captures the account form, which should carry the operations persona and 'Operator Profile' header rather than John Doe / ThemeSelection defaults.
mobile_sidebar_open captures the vertical sidebar toggled open at 390px, exposing the 'Ternpoint Ops' brand wordmark and the renamed 'Operations' primary nav entry.

Source inspection confirms the app is a Laravel + Vite + Blade Materio template whose demo copy lives in a handful of Blade views, the menu JSON, and config/variables.php, with static image assets served from public/assets.
desktop_dispatch_rail scrolls the dispatch-rail into view on the dashboard footer so its metric tiles, shift-band buttons, and readout are captured; this is the visual-regression anchor.
desktop_rail_afternoon and desktop_rail_night click the Afternoon and Night shift-band buttons respectively (changed_from desktop_dispatch_rail) and capture the re-synced readout.
desktop_basic_cards and desktop_buttons must show the same shared dispatch-rail in the footer, confirming cross-page presence.

change_completion: The dashboard hero, Work Orders card, Fleet Utilization panel, Jobs by Region panel, and small metric cards all read as one coherent dispatch-operations surface.
The Zipcar/Bitbank/Aviato brands, the Sales by Countries panel, and the John Doe / ThemeSelection account defaults no longer appear on the captured routes.
The sidebar brand, the renamed Operations nav entry, the account Operator Profile persona, and the rebranded metadata are all present and consistent.
The cards, charts, tables, forms, and sidebar/navbar chrome remain functional after the edits.
The shared Shift dispatch cadence rail renders on every route with its metric tiles, shift-band buttons, and live readout.
Clicking Afternoon/Night re-syncs the readout to the selected band.
design_consistency: The rebrand preserves Materio's Bootstrap 5 sidebar/navbar/card layout, spacing, typography, and light palette.
New copy is restrained, credible field-service operations content that fits the existing card and form structure.
The result remains a Bootstrap admin dashboard, not a marketing or redesigned site.
The dispatch-rail uses Materio's light rounded card styling and stays visually consistent across pages.
regression: All sidebar menu entries, dashboard routes, the cards/basic and ui/buttons pages, and the account-settings form remain reachable with no console or network errors.
The primary nav rename from Dashboards to Operations preserves its route, and the Ternpoint Ops brand wordmark still renders in the sidebar.
The dispatch-rail appears on the cards and buttons reference pages, not just the dashboard.
responsive: 390px dashboard and the opened mobile sidebar have no horizontal overflow or collided controls.
The dashboard cards, sidebar, navbar, and account form wrap cleanly on mobile.
The dispatch-rail metric row wraps with no horizontal overflow at 390px.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Laravel + Blade + Bootstrap 5 Materio admin template rebranded into the Ternpoint Ops field-service dispatch operations console. L4 design_continuity Edit: alongside the multi-surface rebrand (hero, Work Orders card, Fleet Utilization panel, Jobs by Region, Operator Profile account persona, Operations sidebar nav, metadata), a shared interactive 'Shift dispatch cadence' rail is injected into the footer so it renders on every route. The rail carries four orthogonal graded axes: a wrapping metric-tile row (no mobile horizontal overflow), a light Materio card skin (visual regression anchor via component crops of the tiles), cross-page presence on the cards and buttons reference pages, and a shift-band button interaction that re-syncs the live readout. Runs via php artisan serve against a Vite-built manifest; asset images under public/assets/img are served locally. Negative controls: the baseline leg ships the rail with a fixed nowrap overflow layout, dashboard-only presence, and correct readout wiring; the bad leg additionally collapses the tiles into a dark slab and binds the readout to a stale value so the shift-band interaction never updates it.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: themeselection materio-bootstrap-html-laravel-admin-template-free is a runnable Laravel + Vite + Bootstrap 5 admin template (Materio) with a polished sidebar/navbar/card dashboard but generic sales/e-commerce demo copy, making it an ideal host for a design_continuity rebrand into a field-service dispatch operations console across the dashboard, account settings, sidebar brand/nav, and metadata while preserving the Bootstrap admin shell.
